summary: Session 1 (architecture decision, no code): recorded the generator-acquisition decision for Dabbler.CrudSlice / Dabbler.SchemaApplicator with a tri-provider verdict (Opus full-context + GPT-5.4 + Gemini 2.5 Pro, self-contained prompts). DECISION: Option A -- publish as a `dotnet tool` on nuget.org (unanimous A), mirroring the existing Dabbler.Security.DevIdp.Tool precedent and reusing the locked single DabblerVersion + pack.ps1 + trusted-publishing path unchanged. Surface: ONE tool now (Dabbler.CrudSlice.Tool / `dabbler-crud-slice`), with Dabbler.SchemaApplicator.Tool pre-named and deferred until a standalone consumer exists (reversibility; CrudSlice bundles SchemaApplicator in-process). Runner-up: Option C (formalize source checkout). Rejected B (library-shape invites <PackageReference>, dragging build-time code into runtime restore -- permanent on public IDs). Key Session-2-binding finding (flagged independently by both routed reviewers): CrudSlice shells out to `dotnet new dabbler-crud-service/-page`, so acquisition is TWO installs at the same pinned version (Dabbler.Templates + the tool) and the clean-machine consumer-validation gate MUST install both. Cross-provider verification (gpt-5-4): VERIFIED, Round 1, no substantive issues. Greenfield pilot: session-start ref aac874e noted; Step-6 matrix correctly deferred to source-bearing Session 2 (operator-confirmed). Owner ratification of the permanent public IDs/commands recommended before Session 2 implements them.

reason.specifics: Session 2 is source-bearing (PackAsTool on CrudSlice, pack.ps1 two-list + solution-filter edits, a checkout-free clean-machine consumer-validation gate, and a cross-repo orchestrator note) AND is the greenfield finding-power pilot LEAD: it runs the Step-6 provider x surface verification matrix before remediation and adjudicates findings against the fixed rubric. A strong orchestrator for that adjudication is warranted; the mechanical packaging portions can still be routed/handled at sonnet-class cost.
